scope: Development and release builds; no library format or protocol change

retention.appCleanup: Existing one-second polling task and snapshot/detail application
retention.countLimits: Existing 200 timeline rows and 900 traffic samples per transfer remain
retention.clock: Wall-clock event timestamps; expired and future timestamps are excluded
retention.deadline: Cleanup can be delayed by scheduling, suspension, long operations or update/quit barriers

behavior: Engine tracker queues expire without inspector requests, including when network policy blocks transfers.
Detail replies omit expired tracker events without resetting event sequence numbers.
App cleanup expires timeline rows, graph samples and cached detail events while its polling task runs.
Delayed detail replies cannot repopulate expired events.
Snapshot removal prunes timeline and graph records independently.
The activity inspector labels its 15-minute window.

runtimeTests.newRegression: Timestamp cutoff, expired/current/future timestamps and saturating subtraction; compiled only

limitations: Saved statistics, resume records, tracker status/error fields, peer caches, notifications and recent documents have separate retention.
No exact erasure deadline, zeroization, secure-erasure or private-session claim.
Backward clock changes can discard future-dated events early.
pending: Expiry without new events, hidden/offline windows and network-blocked engines
Delayed replies, removed transfers and event sequence continuity
Clock changes, sleep/wake, long operations and update barriers
